operations.value:
Add an opt-in change log to the CLI so a person or agent can review how a task reached its current state and compare any two points in its history. Plain workbook show is unchanged; workbook show <id> --history lists changes, and workbook show <id> --compare <commit> <commit> renders a field-level diff between two points. Entries are one per operation pack rather than one per operation, because actor, wall time, and logical clock are all pack-level and 243 of this project's 258 packs carry exactly one operation. A pack touching several fields renders as one row naming them, "changed title and status". Address entries by commit object ID rather than by a synthesized identifier: reconciliation parks pre-replay commits under refs/workbook/reconciled/<task-id>/<n>, so an object named by an earlier listing stays reachable, and no operation-pack format change is needed here.

Order the list by the parent chain, not by wall time, and print wall time as attribution only. Replay preserves an operation's wall time while rewriting its logical clock, so after a reconciliation the two orders legitimately disagree. Show what the chain says and let the timestamps read out of order rather than reordering them; that disagreement is the visible fingerprint of replayed work and is the signal this view exists to carry. Diff the two --compare arguments in the order given, the way git diff does, and never sort them, since operation ULIDs sort by authoring time and no longer track chain position once a task has been reconciled.

Default to the ten most recent changes, with --limit <n> and --all. When entries are omitted, say so: "Showing 10 most recent changes out of 200". Render each field in its own terms. Title, status, and priority read as old to new. Rank reads as "Reordered" with no values, because a rank is opaque and its literal value tells a reader nothing. Description is the only field needing a real diff, so compute a word-level diff in Go and emit spans. Add no JavaScript dependency and no build step for it: the library at diffs.com is @pierre/diffs, React on top of Shiki, a source-code syntax highlighter, which fits neither a self-contained vanilla-JS asset served offline nor a Go binary with four direct module dependencies, and WB-01KZ24RAMB8QYSWZAYZXNZ25FX needs the same diff in Go regardless.

Serve the list from the SQLite projection through a new operations table. Key rows on operation ULID rather than commit object ID: replay preserves operation ULIDs and rewrites logical clocks, which rewrites every downstream object ID, so a ULID-keyed row survives a reconciliation and only its ordering and object-ID columns change. Store operations alone and reconstruct any state by replaying from the root through core.Apply; --compare replays both endpoints in full. Do not store per-row state checkpoints. Measure that cost once it exists and add checkpoints only if measurement demands them.

The current refresh path cannot fill that table. refreshChangedHeads compares cached tips to current tips and reads only the changed tips, which is complete for current state and blind to the intermediate commits an operation table needs; a fetch advancing a task twelve commits yields one new tip and eleven unread packs. Refresh each changed task by walking its previous head to its new head through ReadTaskHistories and its StopAt boundary, and reproject full histories on rebuild. Projection refresh and rebuild now scale with operation count rather than task count, so this work owns the resulting projection_refresh benchmark regression and re-baselines it from measured evidence rather than guessing a budget.

Stop validating every commit inside ReadTaskHistories on this read path. Write-path validation already prevents this clone from recording an invalid commit, and setup, sync, and fetch validate what arrives from elsewhere, so revalidating a whole history on every read buys nothing and makes a read scale with history depth. When a commit is unreadable, truncate softly: return the valid prefix, name the boundary commit, and let show print what it has plus the truncation rather than failing the whole read. Where the projection holds no operations for a task, fall back to a bounded Git read so show still answers.

In --json, nest history inside task, gate it behind the same flag, and omit the member entirely when it is not requested so today's consumers see an unchanged shape. Verification state is not a rendering concern, because setup, sync, and fetch validate and any unverified row is transient. If a join against the validation cache is ever wanted, cache.sqlite and validation.sqlite already sit together in <common-git-dir>/workbook/, so ATTACH suffices and neither cache needs merging; they stay separate files so a ValidatorVersion bump does not force a projection rebuild and a long validation pass does not hold the SQLite writer lock against mutations.

Out of scope: every web surface, tracked in WB-01KZ94M9AE2D98V7P08YPYCF49; a status lifecycle lane, which belongs with that web treatment, since status dominates the corpus but a single task takes roughly four status changes across its whole life and does not dominate one task's log; undo, which is an ordinary additive inverse operation needing no history machinery; selectively discarding local work before publishing; range syntax for --compare; per-row state checkpoints; and any operation-pack format change, including a pack identifier or replay provenance, which commit-object addressing removes the need for here.
